system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Cole Corporate Income Trust, Inc. realized record, fixed ~2016-2018 window

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window is fixed at 3-5 years after
> ~2013 (i.e. ~2016-2018). Because the registrant was acquired and deregistered in early
> 2015, there is no in-window standalone public annual report; the traceable realized
> record is drawn from the closing-era vote/press 8-K and the deregistration Form 15. This
> sub-dossier contains no information about how the earlier acquisitions were structured.

## Public-reporting status within the outcome window
- The registrant's final standalone annual report was the Form 10-K for fiscal year ended
  December 31, 2013 (accession 0001490626-14-000006, filed 2014-03-31); no Form 10-K was
  filed for any fiscal year after 2013. [SRC: SEC accession 0001490626-14-000006, Form 10-K] [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001490626&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40]
- Consequently there is no audited public financial statement for the registrant covering
  the fixed ~2016-2018 outcome window; the facts below rely on the registrant's own
  closing-era 8-K, its attached press release, and its Form 15 deregistration. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-15-005758, Form 15-12G]

## Realized liquidity event (merger into Select Income REIT)
- The registrant entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated August 30, 2014 with
  Select Income REIT ("SIR") and SC Merger Sub, LLC ("SIR Merger Sub"), a wholly owned
  subsidiary of SIR, providing for the registrant to merge with and into SIR Merger Sub,
  with SIR Merger Sub surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of SIR. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-021749, Form 8-K Item 5.07]
- At a special meeting held January 27, 2015 (record date December 12, 2014, with
  197,605,729 shares outstanding), stockholders approved the merger by 120,005,549.10 for,
  5,659,664.95 against, and 3,635,589.03 abstaining; the press release stated approximately
  92.8% of shares voted were in favor, representing approximately 60.7% of all eligible
  shares. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-021749, Form 8-K Item 5.07 + EX-99.1]
- Merger consideration: each registrant share entitled the holder to elect either $10.50 in
  cash or 0.36 SIR common shares, subject to a limitation that neither the cash nor the
  share consideration exceed 60.0% of the total; registrant stockholders were expected to
  own approximately 32% of SIR's outstanding shares based on a 60% cash election. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-021749, Form 8-K EX-99.1]
- By this date the registrant was described as "a public, non-listed REIT managed by Cole
  Capital," Cole Capital being "the private capital management business of American Realty
  Capital Properties, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARCP)" — i.e. the external manager's ultimate parent was
  then ARCP; the registrant had completed a $2.0 billion capital raise in September 2013.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-021749, Form 8-K EX-99.1]

## Consummation and deregistration (end of standalone public existence)
- On January 30, 2015 a Form 15 (Rule 12g-4(a)(1) / 12h-3(b)(1)(i)) was filed by "SC Merger
  Sub LLC (as successor to Cole Corporate Income Trust, Inc.)," c/o Select Income REIT, Two
  Newton Place, Newton, Massachusetts, certifying termination of registration of the common
  stock under Section 12(g); the approximate number of holders of record as of the notice
  date was 1. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-15-005758, Form 15-12G]
- The successor designation and single holder of record establish that the registrant was
  absorbed into SIR and ceased to file periodic reports thereafter; no subsequent periodic
  or annual report appears on its EDGAR record. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-15-005758, Form 15-12G] [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001490626&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40]

## Disclosed integration risk factors (forward-looking, not realized outcomes)
- The January 27, 2015 communication cautioned that "costs or difficulties related to the
  integration of SIR's and CCIT's operations will be greater than expected," that "operating
  costs and disruption of management's attention from ongoing business operations may be
  greater than expected," and noted risks to relationships with customers, tenants, and
  lenders; these are stated risk factors, not documented realized results. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-021749, Form 8-K EX-99.1]

## Outcome coding
- Within the fixed ~2016-2018 outcome window there is NO standalone public record for the
  registrant: it merged into Select Income REIT and deregistered in January 2015, and the
  acquirer did not separately disclose the former registrant's standalone portfolio
  trajectory in that window. The in-window realized outcome is therefore coded
  **UNCERTAIN (no public standalone record)**; the last documented realized event is the
  early-2015 acquisition by SIR at $10.50 cash / 0.36 SIR share per registrant share. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-15-005758, Form 15-12G] [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-15-021749, Form 8-K EX-99.1]

[SLICE END]
